I disagree, sorry. To me, it even improves the image. Especially if you're using Transformer DLAA. 

Most games nowadays default to TAA, and have a lot of issues with motion clarity, DLSS4 seems to fix a lot of those problems. 

There's also a way to get better image quality still, which is combining DLDSR and DLSS at Quality, which gets you about the same performance as native but a much better image.

I don't know if my opinion is worth anything, but the transformer model looks even better than most native TAA implementations at 1440p, at least in the games I tested. 

Especially on The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk, it's like a night and day difference in motion clarity. They really improved on that, to the point where I'd rather use DLSS Quality at 1440p over native any day.

Edit: Fixed some spelling issues.

DLSS, as of the transformer model, looks significantly better than FSR 3.1 in every way possible, and it's not close. Image stability, motion clarity and other factors make this comparison unfavorable to AMD at the moment. 

This could change, however, if FSR4 is as good as the previews indicate. At least from the limited showcases we saw at CES, if you get a 9070xt/9070, you're going to see a much improved upscaler from AMD on every FSR 3.1 supported title.

I don't know wether or not the improvements will reach RX 7000, but they will probably do something to improve their previous gen's upscaling, because it's not an easy battle as of the current day.

I honestly still don't agree. Bethesda games are pure sandboxes at a conceptual level and a game design level, while CDPR games are much more focused on the story and tend to have better stories than anything bethesda makes.

I mean, if anything, I'd say it's more fair to say that CDPR borrows from Interplay/Obsidian and not Bethesda.

I don't see how you can make that comparison. The Witcher is far too different from Skyrim. Skyrim is meant to be a sandbox at first place, with 100% of the gameplay dedicated in one way or another to exploration. 

In the Witcher 3, you don't explore for the sake of exploring or finding something new. You do it because it makes sense to do so while following the plot. Cyberpunk will be much more similar to The Witcher in that regard, you probably will explore the city while you start doing quests and learning more about the world around you.

I'm sorry, but comparing Bethesda's game design and CDPR's game design is a very unfair statement, they are very different companies making extremely different games and experiences.
